name: Testicular Teratoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Testicular Teratoma

criteria.description: Histological identification of teratomatous elements (ectodermal, mesodermal, endodermal tissues) in testicular tumor biopsy or orchiectomy specimen
Ultrasound showing heterogeneous intratesticular mass with cystic and solid components
Normal or mildly elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels, distinguishing from other germ cell tumors

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of teratomatous tissue plus characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Serum tumor markers help differentiate teratoma from other non-seminomatous germ cell tumors.

searchTerms: feeling of heaviness or discomfort in testicle

common.symptomName: Palpable intratesticular mass on physical exam

searchTerms: lower back pain from swollen lymph nodes
back pain due to deep abdominal lymph node enlargement
pain in lower back from lymph node swelling

occasional.symptomName: Lower extremity edema secondary to lymphatic obstruction
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to lymph obstruction

rare.symptomName: Acute scrotal pain due to tumor infarction or hemorrhage
searchTerms: testis pain due to bleeding or infarction

rare.symptomName: Metastatic symptoms such as cough or hemoptysis
searchTerms: symptoms from cancer spread like cough
lung symptoms due to cancer spread

laboratory: Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) normal or mildly elevated
Serum beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) normal or mildly elevated
imaging: Scrotal ultrasound showing heterogeneous mass with cystic and solid areas
CT scan of abdomen/pelvis for staging and lymph node assessment
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic chromosomal abnormalities may be present in germ cell tumors
other: Histopathology demonstrating mature and/or immature tissues from multiple germ layers

distinguishingFeatures: Histology showing uniform cells with clear cytoplasm
Histology with primitive epithelial cells and high mitotic rate

redFlags: Presence of metastatic symptoms such as cough or back pain
Elevated serum tumor markers inconsistent with teratoma
